expected.arithmetic: This is a scorecard task. Use only the designated scorecard. Take each group's score for the 'on' setting, weight it by that group's share of the target mix, and add the weighted scores to get a total for 'on'. Repeat the same steps with the 'off' scores to get a total for 'off'. Choose whichever setting has the higher total.
expected.context: Suppose you have to advise on whether switching a certain setting on would raise the success rate in a target population. Everyone in that population belongs to one of two groups, and which group a person is in is settled before any treatment happens. You have two sources of evidence. One study handed out the setting at random, so chance decided who got it. The other is a historical study where operators chose the setting themselves, and there may be risk factors nobody measured that pushed both their choice and the eventual outcome, so that evidence can mislead. You can assume the effect of the setting inside each group carries over unchanged to the target population. What differs is the share of people in each group, and that mix will be shown to you. The calculation is left to you: work out what turning the setting on would do for success in this population.

Giving the arithmetic formula separated the sign of a numerical estimate from the explicitly selected action. Single-fence handling mattered to the result.
Disabling CPU repacking did not rescue Q2 output. Repeated items checked operational reproducibility and added no independent families.
The larger F16 reference missed the competence gate on direct prompts. That gate constrained interpretation of a weaker format.
Supplying randomized and historical rates made source selection explicit. Action preference and tree-model misfit complicated the conflict-penalty interpretation.
Q8 reproduced the strong F16 sign performance on the reused formula tasks. Signs and actions remained separate endpoints.

An interrupted F16 run was retained. Completed order arms, rather than partial-run scores with unattempted items, supplied the order comparison.
Interleaving both evidence orders reduced the between-run confound. An early summary halved success and activation counts. Corrected counts preserve paired effects.
The 3B order pattern recurred on new numerical families. The family-bootstrap analysis followed earlier observations. The original count underreporting was corrected.

discrepancies.verified_ground_truth: Repaired canonical JSONs + *_v1_undercounted_counts.json preserved. Family-level contrasts & bootstrap CIs unchanged.

discrepancies.title: Cohort 016 Retrospective Smaller-Gap Magnitude Shortcut

discrepancies.verified_ground_truth: Retrospective audit found |tau| in [0.06, 0.12) < |delta_obs| in [0.38, 0.46) on every item, so choosing the sign of the smaller printed gap solves 768/768 prompts without reading provenance.
